text.p: These are some of the main stories in Sofia newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
TRUD
-- Bulgaria's new parliament assembles today for its first session after April 19 general elections.

The anti-communist Union of Democratic Forces (UDF) and its allies won a clear majority, the former ruling Socialists are the main opposition and three smaller parties and coalitions also entered the parliament.
-- The Bulgarian National Bank (BNB) filed an insolvency suit against the private Capitalbank at the Sofia City Court. The BNB decided to seek Capitalbank bankruptcy on March 27.
24 CHASA
-- The UDF leader and the likely next premier Ivan Kostov said he would aim at continuity of pro-reform policies launched by the interim cabinet of Prime Minister Stefan Sofianski.
-- Bulgaria's caretaker government liberalised domestic prices for petrol and diesel fuel in line with pledges to international financial institutions made earlier this year.
KONTINENT

-- Bulgaria's interior ministry said explosives found near the Sofia airport last week were not intended for an attack on Bulgaria's President Petar Stoyanov and his Romanian counterpart Emil Constantinescu.
-- Bulgaria is expected to seal today the contract for the sale of 70 percent of Devnya Cement plant to Bulgarian-Spanish consortium Marvex, Bulgaria's privatisation agency said.
STANDART

-- Joint ventures registered in Bulgaria would be allowed to buy land in the country regardless of foreign stake in the ventures under draft amendments to the Foreign Investment Act, the head of Bulgaria's Foreign Investment Agency Ilian Vasilev said.
-- Syria may pay its $14 million debt to Bulgaria in durum wheat deliveries, Bulgaria's trade minister Daniela Bobeva said.
PARI
-- The regional court in Dobrich postponed ruling on an insolvency case against private Dobrudzha Bank for June 17.

-- The British Rover Group expects for the new government to negotiate free trade zones with Romania, Russia and Ukraine in order to resume car production in Bulgaria, the head of Bulgaria's Foreign Investment Agency Ilian Vasilev said.

-- The French dairy company Danone plans to buy 550,000 shares of the Bulgarian dairy firm Serdika-1 for around 5.5 billion levs, said Penyo Penev, head of Joint Ventures department at the Agriculture ministry.
NOVINAR
-- The government raised pension payments for June by 16 percent from May levels. The maximum pension will be 56,900 levs, the lowest 24,300 levs.
-- Bulgarian customs in Rousse seized on Tuesday six kg of morphine hidden in the fuel tank of a German-registrated car travelling to Romania.
